Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the final session of Day 2. Indian players are seen in a huddle near the ropes before they disperse. They are joined by two West Indies openers. Tagenarine Chanderpaul and Kraigg Brathwaite will open the innings for West Indies. Mohammed Siraj will start with the new ball for India. Off we go...
... SECOND INNINGS ...

As far as the West Indies are concerned, except for the second session on Day 1 where they got four wickets, they were pretty flat in the field. Kraigg Brathwaite opted to take the second new ball straightaway on Day 2 but failed to get any early breakthrough. That said, they did manage to keep the runs in check and were rewarded with the wickets of Kohli and Jadeja in the second half of the first session. In the post-Lunch session, it was Jason Holder who led the way for the hosts as he accounted for Ishan Kishan. Having done the hard work across two days, Jomel Warrican dealt twin blows and removed Jaydev Unadkat and Mohammed Siraj. In the end, Kemar Roach wrapped India's innings by foxing Ashwin with a slower delivery. For West Indies, the onus is now on the batting unit to put up a much-improved display and fight their way back into the game. Will Kraigg Brathwaite and Co. rise to the challenge? We shall find out when the play resumes in the third and final session of Day 2 in about 20 minutes from now.

SESSION SUMMARY: 65 runs, 20 overs, 4 wickets. India have been bowled out in their first innings for 438! That will also be Tea on Day 2!  Having begun the day at the score of 288-4, the visitors have added 150 runs and lost 6 wickets in the process. India's two overnight batters, Virat Kohli and Ravindra Jadeja, got India off to a confident start on Day 2. Kohli's 121 and Jadeja's 61 helped India remain in a commanding position at the Lunch interval. Ishan Kishan made his intentions clear straightaway, but a loose shot led to his downfall. In the second session, as he has so often done against the West Indies, Ravichandran Ashwin's batting prowess came to the fore and his entertaining knock of 56 runs, helped India stretch their first-innings score to over 400.

OUT! Kemar Roach wraps up India's inning and Ravichandran Ashwin's good inning lower down the order comes to an end! This is bowled on a good length and at the stumps. Ravichandran Ashwin looks to make room and throws the kitchen sink at the ball but does not connect. The ball goes onto peg back the leg pole and India have been bowled out before Tea. They have got a decent total on the board but West Indies will be proud of their effort on a wicket that was conducive for the batters. It will also be TEA on DAY 2!

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set for the afternoon session of Day 2 as the umpires make their way out to the middle. The West Indies players are in a huddle at the boundary line for a few last-minute instructions from Kraigg Brathwaite before taking their respective positions on the field. Ishan Kishan and Ravichandran Ashwin are the two batters for India who stride out to the pitch. Shannon Gabriel has the ball in his hand and is ready to begin proceedings. Let's go...
... DAY 2, SESSION 2 ...

West Indies lacked the cutting edge this morning and looked pretty flat on a surface that had very little to offer. They took the new ball straight away and it allowed the Indian batters to accumulate runs with ease. Both Virat Kohli and Ravindra Jadeja were keen to take risky runs and one cost them dearly when Alzarri Joseph got a direct hit to break the partnership. Kemar Roach worked hard and was rewarded with the wicket but West Indies still have loads of work to do if they are to stake a claim on this tie. Will they be able to wrap up the Indian inning in the afternoon session? Or will India consider a declaration after getting some quick runs? We shall find out shortly. While the players take Lunch, you can switch tabs and catch the action in the Ashes where England have Australia on the back foot in the quest to level the series. Do join us back here at 10.10 pm IST (4.40 pm GMT) for the start of the second session on Day 2.

SESSION SUMMARY - 85 runs and 2 wickets in 24 overs. This session has been shared by the two sides with West Indies dismissing both the set overnight batters but the visitors accumulated 85 runs to get their score to  373 for the loss of 6 wickets. India looked absolutely comfortable for more than an hour as Virat Kohli reached his 29th Test century and Ravindra Jadeja got to his half-century in the same over. The two of them added 159 runs for the fifth wicket in 286 deliveries before the Virat ran himself out on 121. Ravindra Jadeja ended up edging one to the keeper but there was some doubt in the replays on whether the bat hit the pad when the ball was passing the edge. Ishan Kishan has played a few good shots so far and along with Ravichandran Ashwin, will look to up the ante in the second session.

Commentary.Commentary: The sun is shining in its full glory and we are all in readiness for the action on Day 2 to commence. Out come the two umpires followed by the West Indies players. They are joined by the two overnight batters of India, Virat Kohli and Ravindra Jadeja. The second new ball is available but will West Indies take it straight away? Yes, they do. Shannon Gabriel has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's play...

PITCH REPORT - Daren Ganga is pitchside to tell us how the strip looks on Day 2 of this second Test match. He is joined by Stacy-Ann King as he tells us there is a bit of grass coming out of the surface. King agrees with him and says that the wicket will be quicker. Adds that it was a bit slow early on Day 1 but then the ball started skidding through and coming onto the bat. Claims that it is a wonderful batting track though and runs will from freely. Mentions that they saw Jomel Warrican nagging the batters with his length and got a number of balls to turn away from the bat which means there is definitely some spin on offer. Ganga ends by saying that on the whole it is still a batting paradise but there could be some help for the spinners and the pacers could come into play on Day 2 due to the grass.

On the other hand, after Kraigg Brathwaite won the toss and opted to bowl first, the West Indies failed to get any success in the first session. The decision to bowl first in good batting conditions seemed to have backfired, but the bowling unit stepped up in the second session to put their side on top. The West Indies bowlers toiled hard in the post-Tea session without much luck. All is not lost for the hosts, though, as the second new ball is due and they would want to make use of the early movement on offer. Can the West Indies fight their way back into the game? We shall find out soon, as the first ball on Day 2 is not far away.

After being put into bat under sunny conditions, the two Indian openers, Rohit Sharma and Yashasvi Jaiswal, picked up where they left off in the first Test and laid a solid foundation by notching their respective fifties. India stuttered a bit in the second session, where they lost four wickets and, for the first time in the series, found themselves on the back foot. Virat Kohli and Ravindra Jadeja then got together and started a repair job for India in the third session, ensuring there were no more hiccups in the day. In his 500th international game, Kohli is now just 13 runs away from his 29th Test hundred and what a stage it will be to achieve it.

Hello and a warm welcome, ladies and gentlemen, to our coverage of Day 2 of the second Test between the West Indies and India at Queen's Park Oval in Port of Spain. It was an absorbing day of red-ball cricket, which saw India dominate the first and third sessions on the opening day of this historic Test to take the ascendancy at the end. The visitors went into Stumps with the score of 288 on the board having lost 4 wickets in 84 overs courtesy of an unbeaten 106-run stand between Virat Kohli and Ravindra Jadeja who are batting on 87 and 36 respectively. Loads of cricket still left in this Test match and we expect every minute of it to be enthralling.
... DAY 2, SESSION 1 ...

Right then, the game has ebbed and flowed in sessions but Day 1 has belonged to the visitors as they dominated through chunks of the game. The wicket looked good for batting and despite the stumble in the afternoon session, India will be hoping to post a massive first-inning total. West Indies will want to start well in the morning session and try and restrict the Indians to under 350. There is more action coming out way on Friday 21st July for Day 2 of this second Test match between India and West Indies. The first ball will be bowled at 7.30 pm IST (2 pm GMT) but you can join us early for the build-up. Cheers!

Shannon Gabriel is up for a chat. He says that it was a tough day for them. Mentions that apart from the first session, the bowlers did well and put the ball in the right areas. Shares that they expected the ball to bounce more but it did not happen. Reckons that they were all over the place in the first session. Adds that they went back and assessed the lengths. Feels that it was all about being patient. Ends by saying that the new ball is due and they will look to be patient on Day 2 for as long as possible.

India were put into bat by Kraigg Brathwaite after winning the toss and it seemed like the move would backfire as India did not lose a single wicket in the first session. Both the Indian openers had got to their half-centuries as they went into Lunch with 121 runs on the board in just 26 overs. West Indies bowlers did toil hard but were unable to execute their plans to perfection. Things did not go as per plan post Lunch for India as they lose Yashasvi Jaiswal early off the bowling of Jason Holder and Shubman Gill's poor run in the series continued as he was dismissed by Kemar Roach soon after.  Rohit Sharma looked good for his 80 till he received a peach of a delivery from Jomel Warrican and found his off pole pegged back. Shannon Gabriel's return to the side turned fruitful as he dismissed Ajinkya Rahane at the stroke of Tea to make it the first session the hosts have won in this series. It was one-way traffic thereafter as normalcy was restored.

SESSION SUMMARY - 106 runs and no wickets in 33.2 overs. India have overcome the disappointment of the afternoon session where they lost four wickets with a commanding display in the final session of Day 1. Virat Kohli was joined by Ravindra Jadeja after Tea with Ajinkya Rahane being dismissed just before the break. The two of them started slow looking to get a read on the pitch and soaked in the pressure. Their patience paid rich dividends as the runs began to flow and the partnership began to build. The two of them played out the entire session and added a 106-run unbeaten partnership for the fifth wicket and India to help their side get back on top in this game. The West Indies bowlers tried really hard but could not find a way to get rid of India's batting pair as the visitors finished on 288 for the loss of four wickets in 84 overs. Virat Kohli is 13 runs short of his century with Ravindra Jadeja closing in on his half-century as well and they will look to press the advantage further on Day 2.

Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the third and final session of Day 1. Out come the West Indies players and so do, the two Indian batters. Ravindra Jadeja is the new batter and he joins Virat Kohli out in the middle. Shannon Gabriel has the ball in hand and he will complete his over. Let's play...
... DAY 1, SESSION 3 ...

Having been in a strong position at the Lunch interval, Rohit Sharma and Yashasvi Jaiswal were watchful in their approach at the start of the second session. Jaiswal, in particular, found it tough to score runs and eventually ran out of both patience and luck to be dismissed on 57. Coming in at number 3, Shubman Gill did employ a positive approach, but he poked away from the body and paid the price. Rohit Sharma fell soon after and missed out on what would have been his third Test hundred away from home. Out of nowhere, India found themselves in a spot of bother at 155-3. Virat Kohli and Ajinkya Rahane then got together and applied themselves well to provide calmness to the Indian innings. Just when it seemed that India were rebuilding nicely, Ajinkya Rahane chopped one back onto the stumps to peg India back once again. Indian fans will be hoping that Virat Kohli bats and bats well to take India to a challenging first-innings total. Who will be in the ascendancy at the end of day's play? We will have all the answers as the players return for the third session at 12.30 am IST (7.00 pm GMT, the previous day).

SESSION SUMMARY: 61 runs, 24.4 overs, and 4 wickets. It was all India in the first session, and the visitors were expected to dominate the second session as well. But the West Indies have come roaring back to win their first session of the series. Having struggled to make a mark with the ball for the entirety of the first session, the West Indies needed to start well in the second session. It was Jason Holder who led the way with probing lines and lengths against Yashasvi Jaiswal. He was rewarded for his persistence as Jaiswal edged one to deep gully. Once the opening stand was broken, it looked like the West Indies had found a spring in their step. The move to bring Kemar Roach back into the attack paid off straight away for Kraigg Brathwaite, as the former got rid of Shubman Gill. Playing as the frontline spinner in the side, Jomel Warrican came to the party as well and got the big wicket of Rohit Sharma. The West Indies bowlers stuck at it and did not allow the Indian batters to release the pressure. In the last over before Tea, Shannon Gabriel went through the defence of Ajinkya Rahane to put his side in a strong position. Kraigg Brathwaite will be hoping for more of the same from his bowling group in the third session.

OUT! CHOPPED ON! Shannon Gabriel gets his first wicket and what a session this has turned out to be for West Indies! Ajinkya Rahane is the latest casualty as he plays a really lazy shot before the break. This is bowled on a good length as well and in the channel outside the off stump. Ajinkya Rahane pokes at the ball with no real intent and gets an inside edge that goes on to shatter his stumps. Rahane looks stunned as India have lost their fourth wicket and have stumbled slightly after the strong start that they had. The hosts have come back really strong in this game and will be going into the dressing room with their tails up as it will be TEA of DAY 1!

The pacers toiled hard but the wicket seemed pretty flat and Kraigg Brathwaite may have made a massive mistake electing to bowl first on this surface. Jason Holder and Jomel Warrican were economical and helped bring some control which almost resulted in a wicket but Alick Athanaze dropped a tough opportunity at slip just before the break. Windies are yet to draw the first blood and it seems like they have a long day on the field in store for them. They will have to come up with better plans and hope to get a few wickets to come back into this game. Can they do it or will India continue on their merry way? We shall find out shortly. While the players take Lunch, you can switch tabs for the 4th Ashes Test where 'Bazball' is in full throttle and Zak Crawley is nearing a fantastic double hundred. Do join us back here at 10.10 pm IST (4.40 pm GMT) for the start of the second session on Day 1.

SESSION SUMMARY - 121 runs and no wickets in 26 overs. A session that has belonged well and truly to the visitors and the hosts have had no response to the early onslaught by India! An excellent couple of hours for Indian openers means that they have posted an unbeaten stand of 121 runs in 26 overs. Rohit Sharma and Yashasvi Jaiswal have been aggressive from the word go and look settled at the wicket having cashed in on the loose balls. They have both gone past their fifties and will be looking to convert this into a big one. The skipper has scored 63 runs in 102 balls and Jaiswal has been really impressive racing to his half-century in just 49 deliveries. India have stamped their authority on this game and will hope to carry on in a similar manner throughout the day as they look to post a substantial first-inning total.

Commentary.Commentary: We are done with pre-game formalities as the two umpires make their way out to the middle. The West Indies players are in a huddle near the ropes before they disperse. They are joined by the two Indian openers. Yashasvi Jaiswal and Rohit Sharma will open the innings for India. Kemar Roach has the new ball in hand and will start the proceedings for the West Indies. Off we go...

We are moments away from the start of the 100th Test between India and West Indies, but before that, it's time for the national anthems. It will be the national anthem of Trinidad and Tobago first, followed by the national anthem of India and then the West Indies. The two captains Kraigg Brathwaite and Rohit Sharma are now presented with memorabilia on the occasion of the 100th Test between India and the West Indies.

PITCH REPORT - Samuel Badree is pitchside and he says that the wicket looks firm and the ball will come onto the bat nicely early in the game. Reckons that as the Test match progresses the spinners will come into play. Adds that there may be a bit for the pace bowlers but it will suit the slower bowlers more.

Rohit Sharma, the skipper of India, says that they were looking to bat first anyway. Adds that it is a decent pitch and the weather is nice and sunny as well. Reckons that the wicket will get slower as the game progresses. Informs that Shardul Thakur misses out due to a niggle. Adds that he will be replaced by Mukesh Kumar who will make his Test debut. Mentions that he is a talented guy and has worked really hard. On the 100th Test between India and West Indies, he says that there are a lot of memories and it has been a good rivalry. Shares that batters have always been required to work hard to get the result here. Ends by saying that there have been a lot of positives from the last game and hopes to continue.

Kraigg Brathwaite, the captain of West Indies, says that they will bowl first and with Shannon Gabriel back, they have a good set of fast bowlers to exploit the conditions. Adds that Kirk Mckenzie makes his debut today and replaces Raymon Reifer. Mentions that bowling wise they were okay and will have to continue the discipline that they showed. Claims that when it comes to the batting, they want to forget the first game and start afresh. Admits that India have some world-class spinners and young fast bowlers but they need to believe in themselves. Feels that it is an honour to play in the 100th Test match and recent years they have not won a match in a while and they want to change that but in the past with the likes of Sachin Tendulkar and Brian Lara, the encounters were unbelievable.

India (Playing XI) - Yashasvi Jaiswal, Rohit Sharma (C), Shubman Gill, Virat Kohli, Ajinkya Rahane, Ravindra Jadeja, Ishan Kishan (WK), Ravichandran Ashwin, Jaydev Unadkat, Mohammed Siraj, Mukesh Kumar (On Test debut) (In for Shardul Thakur).

West Indies (Playing XI) - Kraigg Brathwaite (C), Tagenarine Chanderpaul, Jermaine Blackwood, Jason Holder, Alick Athanaze, Joshua Da Silva (WK), Kirk Mckenzie (In for Rahkeem Cornwall), Alzarri Joseph, Kemar Roach, Jomel Warrican, Shannon Gabriel (In for Raymon Reifer).
TOSS - The two captains are out in the middle. The coin toss lands in the favour of Kraigg Brathwaite and the West Indies have opted to BOWL first.

As far as India are concerned, it was a perfect game for Rohit Sharma's men, and they will be hoping to put in a similar performance in this game as well. In favourable conditions, the spin twins Ravichandran Ashwin and Ravindra Jadeja weaved their magic to bowl the West Indies out twice in three days. With the bat, Yashasvi Jaiswal and Rohit Sharma notched respective centuries, but Virat Kohli fell 24 runs short of a hundred. Playing in his 500th international game, Kohli would want to make this occasion even more special by reaching the three-figure mark. Will India's dominance help them make it 2-0? Or will we see the West Indies fight back in this historic Test? Let's find out. Toss and team news coming up shortly...

At Windsor Park, the West Indies failed to show up in both departments and as a result, they suffered an innings defeat at the hands of India. If they are to make a comeback in this series, Kraigg Brathwaite and Co. will need to start afresh by putting that loss behind them. The hosts were let down by their batting unit and will be required to put their hands up in this game. Having failed to make a mark in the first Test, the Caribbean pacers might come into play this time around.

After India's dominant win inside three days at Dominica, the two teams have now made the trip to Port of Spain for the second Test. Queen's Park Oval is all decked up to host what is going to be the 100th Test between the two sides. Hello and a warm welcome, ladies and gentlemen, to our coverage of Day 1 of the second Test between the West Indies and India at Queen's Park Oval in Port of Spain.
